A difference-in-differences design from pre-treatment pilot data

Source: R/did-pilot.R
ape_dgp_did_pilot.Rd

Estimates, from data observed before the treatment date, the inputs of ape_dgp_did() that such data can inform, and builds the design:

Usage

ape_dgp_did_pilot(data, outcome, group, id = NULL, period = NULL, trend, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame of pre-treatment observations.

outcome, group

Names of the binary outcome and of the indicator of the group that will be treated (0/1 or logical).

id

Optional name of the unit identifier. With it the design is a panel and rho is estimated (units need two or more periods); without it the design is repeated cross-sections.

period

Optional name of the period variable; used to report the control group's change between pre-treatment periods.

trend

The control group's change in the outcome rate from before to after treatment, in probability points. Required.

...

Further arguments of ape_dgp_did(), such as model, n_pre, n_post, trends, analysis, covariates. Naming baseline, gap, p_treated, rho or design here overrides the estimate. A subgroup is not supported.

Value

A powerape_dgp as from ape_dgp_did(), with the estimates and the pilot's size in $pilot. Pin the effect with set_att().

Details

  • baseline: the control group's outcome rate;

  • gap: the treated group's rate minus the control group's;

  • p_treated: the share of units (rows, without id) in the treated group;

  • rho, for a panel: the latent within-unit correlation of the route's Gaussian copula, by the method of moments (the value at which the model's probability of the outcome in two periods of one unit equals the observed share of such pairs).

All pre-treatment periods are pooled, because the route holds rates flat before the treatment date. Pre-treatment data cannot tell how the control group will change from before to after treatment, so trend must be supplied; when the pilot has several periods, the control group's average change from one to the next is reported as a guide. Covariates are not taken from the pilot: pass them as pa_var() objects.

The estimates are used as if they were known. They are not: vary them with ape_robust() (baseline, gap, rho, p_treated), in particular for a small pilot.

Examples

## a pilot panel: 300 units observed in two pre-treatment periods
set.seed(1)
u <- rnorm(300)
treated <- rbinom(300, 1, 0.5)
pilot <- data.frame(
  firm = rep(1:300, 2), year = rep(1:2, each = 300),
  treated = rep(treated, 2),
  y = rbinom(600, 1, pnorm(-0.7 + 0.3 * rep(treated, 2) + 0.8 * rep(u, 2))))
d <- suppressWarnings(
  ape_dgp_did_pilot(pilot, outcome = "y", group = "treated", id = "firm",
                    period = "year", trend = 0.05, model = "logit"))
d <- set_att(d, 0.08)
d
#> powerape DGP -- logit, difference-in-differences (two periods)
#>   data: panel, both periods per unit; rho = 0.40 (latent within-unit correlation); unit-clustered SEs
#>   analysis: pooled logit; ATT = average partial effect of the treatment indicator over treated post-period rows
#>   treated group: 49% of units
#>   covariates: none
#>   untreated trends: parallel on the logit index (the scale the logit analysis assumes)
#>   rates before -> after: control 0.322 -> 0.372; treated 0.385 -> 0.519 (0.439 without treatment)
#>   pilot: baseline, gap, treated share, rho estimated from 600 pre-treatment rows (300 units); control group's change between pilot periods +0.000
#>   true ATT pinned at +0.0800 (treatment coefficient = 0.3213)
#>   the same four rates read under linear-parallel trends: +0.0834 (their cross difference)
